ostrzezenia.tekst: Pressure canning is the only recommended method for canning meat, poultry, seafood and vegetables; using a boiling-water bath for these foods poses a real risk of botulism poisoning.
NCHFP recommends canning low-acid foods, and tomatoes and tomato products, only according to the procedures in the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning.
NCHFP says not to add noodles or other pasta, rice, flour, cream, milk or other thickening agents to home-canned soups.
Penn State Extension says there are no scientifically tested recipes for canning broccoli or cauliflower as a plain vegetable.
Penn State Extension says that broccoli, cauliflower, cabbage, kohlrabi and Brussels sprouts are not suitable for pressure canning.

akapity: Most mixtures of low-acid and acid foods are also low-acid, unless the recipe has enough lemon juice, citric acid or vinegar to make them acid foods.
JarAtlas does not treat a dish as an acid food because it tastes sour, or because acid was added without a tested recipe.
The NCHFP recipe for mixed vegetables does not allow leafy greens, dried beans, cream-style corn, winter squash, sweet potatoes, broccoli, cauliflower or cabbage as substitutes.
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for canned bigos from a checked source.
